We remark that there is a gap between the upper and lower bounds for the mixed margin condition. This situation is analogous to one that persisted in the active learning literature for a number of years (Hanneke, 2014), and was resolved by the work of Hanneke and Yang (2015), establishing that the lower bound is sharp. We conjecture that a similar resolution is possible for reliable active apprenticeship learning under the mixed margin condition (though this may require a different algorithm). Conjecture 18 We conjecture the optimal query complexity of reliable active apprenticeship learning under the mixed margin condition always matches the lower bound in Theorem 12 up to log factors: that is, an upper bound holds, matching the lower bound up to a factor polylog(T, |Π|, 1/δ). 7. Conclusions and Future Directions We have proposed a new learning setting, termed reliable active apprenticeship learning, and established near-optimal query complexity guarantees, under increasingly-general noise models: realizable, Massart, and mixed-margin. A number of important future directions remain open. Perhaps the clearest question is the extension to the agnostic setting, where there are no assumptions on the oracle. A primary challenge in such a setting is even to formulate what kind of reliability requirement is possible.
